title: “NOT MANY WERE WISE.”
paragraphs: “NOT MANY WERE WISE.”

That’s not an insult.
It’s an indictment.
Paul looks at the church in Corinth — a city drunk on philosophy, status, influence — and says:
“Not many of you were wise according to worldly standards. Not many were powerful. Not many were of noble birth.” (1 Corinthians 1:26)
Pause.
Feel that.

God didn’t build His Church with influencers.
He built it with interruptions.
And here’s the open loop you don’t want to ignore:

If God chooses the weak…
why do we spend our lives trying to look strong?

Corinth was a flex culture.
Pedigree mattered. Eloquence mattered. Platform mattered.
But Heaven had a different metric.
“God chose what is foolish in the world to shame the wise; God chose what is weak in the world to shame the strong.” (1 Corinthians 1:27)
Chosen.

Not tolerated.
Not barely accepted.
Chosen.
Let me talk to the one who feels disqualified.

The addict who relapsed.
The leader who failed privately.
The student who thinks they’re not smart enough.
The believer who whispers, “I should be further by now.”
Listen to your pastor’s heart:
God builds with broken tools.

Not because He enjoys dysfunction.
But because when cracked hands hold holy fire, no one mistakes the Source.
The cross itself looked like weakness.

A beaten body.
Sweat and blood mingled.
Breath collapsing under Roman brutality.
Nails through nerve and tendon.
Weak.
Or so they thought.
But what looked like defeat was divine strategy.
“For the word of the cross is folly to those who are perishing, but to us who are being saved it is the power of God.” (1 Corinthians 1:18)
Here is the scandal:

Your weakness is not your disqualification.
Your pride is.

The Gospel does not say, “Clean yourself up and then come.”
It says, “Boast only in the Lord.” (1 Corinthians 1:31)
Some scholars interpret Paul’s language as a direct confrontation against Greek rhetorical elitism — but the Spirit’s message still stands: God refuses to share His glory with human ego.

So He chooses the overlooked.
The unimpressive.
The trembling.
Why?
“So that no human being might boast in the presence of God.” (1 Corinthians 1:29)

This is not about celebrating weakness.
It’s about exposing false strength.
Because in Christ —

Your insecurity becomes dependence.
Your failure becomes repentance.
Your repentance becomes restoration.
And your restoration becomes a testimony that silences the wise.
And here’s the Gospel anchor:
“Because of Him you are in Christ Jesus, who became to us wisdom from God, righteousness and sanctification and redemption.” (1 Corinthians 1:30)

Not self-made wisdom.
Not earned righteousness.
Not self-help redemption.
Jesus.

Sin made you weak.
Grace makes you His.
So stop hiding the cracks.

Bring them to the Cross.
Lay them down.
Repent where pride has ruled.
Receive where shame has shouted.

God is not looking for polished vessels.
He is looking for surrendered ones.
And if you feel like a broken tool in the Builder’s hand…
You are exactly the kind He uses.
